findings.evidence: Lines 146–209 expose the construction body, while lines 211–218 provide the complete pointwise equation consumers need.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; retain the pointwise simp theorem, proving it internally with `:= (rfl)` if needed.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` makes the full proof-built body of `tangentToLeftInvariantDerivation` unfoldable downstream even though `tangentToLeftInvariantDerivation_apply` already characterizes its behavior.

findings.evidence: The declaration at lines 231–239 is public, and `rg` finds no corresponding `_apply` lemma.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem tangentToLeftInvariantDerivationLinear_apply (v) : tangentToLeftInvariantDerivationLinear v = tangentToLeftInvariantDerivation v := (rfl)`.
findings.issue: The public `tangentToLeftInvariantDerivationLinear` has no application theorem, so downstream code cannot normalize its opaque coercion to `tangentToLeftInvariantDerivation`.

findings.evidence: Lines 257–264 define the forward map as that composite, but the sole API theorem at lines 267–279 covers only `.symm`.
findings.fix: Add a `[simp]` forward-application theorem stating that the equivalence applied to `D` equals `pointDerivationEquivTangentSpace 1 BoundarylessManifold.isInteriorPoint (LeftInvariantDerivation.evalAt 1 D)`.
findings.issue: The canonical equivalence is characterized only on its inverse; its forward application remains opaque, preventing users from rewriting it to evaluation at `1` followed by `pointDerivationEquivTangentSpace`.

summary: The construction exposes its implementation despite having a pointwise API, while two public linear maps lack characteristic application lemmas.
